questions.question: Checking your own credit score…
questions.explanation: Checking your own score is a soft search. Lenders can't see it and it doesn't affect your score.

questions.question: Hard search vs soft search:
options: A hard search is visible to lenders and can affect your score; a soft one isn't
Soft searches are only for mortgages
questions.explanation: Hard searches happen when you apply for credit. Soft searches include eligibility checks.

questions.question: Being on the electoral roll…
questions.explanation: Lenders use it to confirm your identity and address.

questions.question: “Credit utilisation” means…
options: How much of your available credit you're using
How often you use your card abroad
questions.explanation: High utilisation can make lenders cautious.

questions.question: Credit limit £2,000, balance £1,800. Your utilisation is…
Section 75 protection applies to credit card purchases costing between…
questions.explanation: Section 75 makes the card provider jointly liable for items or services costing £100–£30,000.

questions.question: For a debit card purchase that goes wrong, the route to ask your bank for money back is…
questions.explanation: Chargeback is a card-scheme process, not a legal right, but banks use it routinely.

questions.question: APR shows…
options: The yearly cost of borrowing, including interest and fees
questions.explanation: APR lets you compare the cost of credit.

questions.question: Only paying the minimum on a credit card each month…
options: Makes the debt take much longer and cost far more
questions.explanation: Minimum payments mostly cover interest, so the debt lingers.

questions.question: A 0% balance transfer card usually charges…
options: A one-off fee, often a few percent of the balance
questions.explanation: Check the transfer fee and how long the 0% lasts.

questions.question: You move £3,000 to a 0% card with a 3% transfer fee, and the 0% lasts 20 months. What monthly payment clears it in time?
When a 0% deal ends, any remaining balance…
options: Starts being charged at the normal rate
questions.explanation: Plan to clear it before the deal ends.

questions.question: Missing a credit card payment can…
options: Hurt your credit file and trigger fees
questions.explanation: Set up at least a minimum-payment Direct Debit.

questions.question: What's the main risk with Buy Now Pay Later?
options: It always charges very high interest
It's easy to overspend, and missed payments can mean fees and debt collection
questions.explanation: BNPL feels painless, which makes it easy to stack up repayments.

questions.question: Payday loans are…
options: Among the most expensive ways to borrow
questions.explanation: Their costs are very high even with the cap.

questions.question: Which usually helps build a thin credit file?
options: Using a credit card a little and paying in full every month
Applying for five cards at once
questions.explanation: Small, regular, fully repaid spending shows you manage credit well.

questions.question: A joint account or joint loan with your partner means…
options: Their credit history can affect how lenders see you
Your neighbours are linked to you
questions.explanation: Joint products create a financial association on your files.

questions.question: If you pay your credit card balance in full every month…
options: You still pay interest on purchases
You usually pay no interest on purchases
questions.explanation: Paying in full avoids purchase interest on most cards.

questions.question: How long do missed payments usually stay on a UK credit file?
questions.explanation: Most records stay for six years.

questions.question: A guarantor loan means…
options: Someone else agrees to repay if you can't
questions.explanation: The guarantor is on the hook, so these loans can strain relationships.

questions.question: Your credit score is based on:
options: Your history of borrowing and repaying, from your credit file
questions.explanation: Scores come from your credit file: repayment history, balances, applications and more.

questions.question: Missed payments can stay on your credit file for:
questions.explanation: Most negative marks, including missed payments and defaults, stay for 6 years.

questions.question: Checking your own credit report:
options: Is free and does not affect it; only applications leave hard searches
questions.explanation: Your own checks are soft searches with no impact; you can check free with all three main agencies.

questions.question: The three main UK credit reference agencies are:
questions.explanation: Each agency holds its own data, so your score can differ between them.

questions.question: Credit utilisation means:
options: The percentage of your available credit you're using; lower is generally better
questions.explanation: Keeping card balances below around 30% of limits is a common guideline for score health.

questions.question: A hard search on your file:
options: Happens every time you check your own report
Happens when you apply for credit and can temporarily lower your score
questions.explanation: Applications leave hard searches; clusters of them suggest risk and can hurt applications.

questions.question: Closing an old, unused credit card can:
options: Shorten your credit history and reduce total available credit, which can hurt your score
Have no possible effect on score
questions.explanation: Long account history and low utilisation both help; closing old cards can remove both.

questions.question: Paying only the minimum on a credit card means:
options: Debt lasts years longer and interest costs balloon
questions.explanation: Minimum payments keep you legal but are designed to stretch debt, and interest, out for years.

questions.question: APR stands for:
options: Annual Percentage Rate: the yearly cost of borrowing including interest and some fees
questions.explanation: APR makes different borrowing costs comparable; lower is cheaper.

questions.question: A card's 'representative APR' applies to:
options: At least 51% of approved applicants, so yours may differ
questions.explanation: Representative means 51% or more of accepted applicants get that rate; others may pay more.

questions.question: A 0% purchase card's main danger is:
options: The deal ends; after that the rate jumps, so have a plan to clear or transfer the balance by then
questions.explanation: 0% deals end; the standard rate afterwards is often very high.

questions.question: Balance transfer cards usually charge:
options: An upfront fee, often a percentage of the amount transferred
questions.explanation: Transfer fees, often around 3%, are part of the real cost comparison.

questions.question: Withdrawing cash on a credit card is usually:
options: Expensive: fees plus immediate interest at high rates, and it can look risky to lenders
questions.explanation: Cash advances start charging interest immediately and often carry fees; avoid if possible.

questions.question: A payday loan is:
options: Very expensive short-term borrowing, capped in cost but still far pricier than alternatives
questions.explanation: Payday loans solve minutes and create months of cost; treat as a last resort.

questions.question: Being on the electoral roll at your current address:
options: Helps lenders verify you and usually supports your credit file
Is required to have a bank account
questions.explanation: Registering to vote is one of the easiest free credit-score improvements.

questions.question: A default on your file means:
options: A creditor has recorded an unpaid debt after formal notices, badly affecting credit for 6 years
questions.explanation: Defaults are serious marks; if one is wrong, dispute it with the agency and creditor.

questions.question: A CCJ (County Court Judgment) for unpaid debt:
options: Is a court order to pay that severely damages credit for 6 years unless settled within a month
Can be avoided by ignoring letters
questions.explanation: Responding to county court letters early can avoid CCJs entirely; ignoring them makes it worse.

questions.question: Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) schemes like Klarna or Clearpay typically:
options: Are recorded on all credit files like loans
Often don't appear on credit files yet, and miss their affordability checks, but regulation is changing this
questions.explanation: BNPL has been light on credit checks and file reporting; treat it as real debt regardless.

questions.question: The risk of stacking multiple BNPL purchases is:
options: Several small repayments become a big monthly commitment with no central view of what you owe
questions.explanation: BNPL's ease hides its weight; track every plan or it bites.

questions.question: A credit builder card typically has:
options: Low limits and high APR, designed to demonstrate repayment behaviour
questions.explanation: Used carefully: spend small, repay in full, and the file improves; used badly, it's expensive.

questions.question: Applying for several credit cards in a short period:
options: Can look desperate to lenders and reduce approval chances
questions.explanation: Space out applications; each leaves a hard search.

questions.question: Lenders see your income directly when you apply:
options: No; credit files don't show income, they ask you and use affordability checks
questions.explanation: Your file shows behaviour, not salary; affordability is assessed from what you declare and bank data where shared.

questions.question: Paying your credit card in full every month:
options: Builds history while costing nothing in interest if there's a grace period
questions.explanation: Full repayment builds a healthy file with zero interest cost.

questions.question: Being a 'financial associate' through a joint mortgage or account means:
options: Their bad credit can affect joint applications, and disassociation takes effort after separation
questions.explanation: Financial links matter; sever them formally after separations so ex-partners' issues don't drag you.

questions.question: Before a mortgage application, you should:
options: Avoid new applications, keep utilisation low, and check all three reports for errors
Miss a payment to test them
questions.explanation: Clean, calm files in the months before an application improve outcomes.

questions.question: Rent payments normally appear on credit files:
options: Only if reported through a rent-reporting scheme, which some renters use to build history
questions.explanation: Rent isn't automatically reported; services can add it if your landlord or platform participates.

questions.question: A prepay card or top-up card usually:
options: Doesn't build credit history because nothing is being borrowed
questions.explanation: No borrowing means no credit history from it.

questions.question: If a debt collector contacts you about a debt you don't recognise, first step:
options: Ask for written details and check your credit reports; don't acknowledge the debt as yours until verified
questions.explanation: Verify before paying; mistaken or fraudulent collections happen, and acknowledgment can restart limitations.
